title.narrative: Protection response in drought affected districts of Sofala and Manica provinces

description.narrative: The objective of this project, which covers the four most drought-affected districts in Sofala and Manica provinces, is to ensure that (i) vulnerable drought-affected people's protection needs/risks are understood by humanitarian and government actors and inform their responses, and that (ii) drought-affected people have access to the protection services they need. Through government partnerships and capacity-building, implementation will be localized, and national systems will be strengthened, ensuring the long-term sustainability of the project beyond the CERF reporting period. The project consists of the following areas of intervention: 1: Protection Monitoring through capacitated local actors In preparation for Protection Monitoring and to establish a baseline of protection knowledge among authorities in the affected districts, UNHCR will contribute to building the capacity of national actors at district and provincial levels. This will include refresher trainings for the Sofala and Manica focal points of Government partner INGD’s Safeguarding Division, namely on protection mainstreaming, identification and referral of people with specific needs (including for cash assistance), and protection-oriented data collection. In addition, INGD will be able to support UNHCR’s capacity-building of other key governmental ministries to mainstream protection across their activities and align with protection principles (including PSEA), identify the protection impact of drought on the population, identify and prioritize people with specific needs in their service provision, case management, co-develop and utilize referral pathways, and ensure accountability to affected people, thus strengthening national systemsFollowing the trainings, UNHCR will support its partner INGD to conduct Protection Monitoring (in the form of four Protection Assessments (one in each district)) amongst 1,600 affected households (around 8,000 persons), utilizing their protection and data collection knowledge gained during the project’s first phase to assess the protection impact of the drought on the population, identify protection risks/needs, humanitarian assistance needs, and plans in the medium- and long-term. This will provide an evidence base to inform multisectoral, interagency programming, both for life-saving emergency interventions, as well as longer-term durable solutions initiatives. The Protection Monitoring will result in four reports (one per district) that will include specific recommendations based on findings, to be widely disseminated among all stakeholders to inform their programming. Community-awareness raising will also be an embedded component of this project, ensuring that affected populations (broken down into the relevant age, gender, and diversity groups) are made aware of available services and assistance, and protection principles and rights. This component will reach up to 7,000 individuals.2: Provision of multi-purpose cash/ in-kind assistance for protectionWorking with INGD and other relevant national actors for the identification and referral of beneficiaries, UNHCR will support 15,800 vulnerable drought-affected people with multi-purpose cash/in-kind assistance (including for transportation costs to reach protection services, costs of civil documentation, medical costs for assistance to GBV survivors, costs of basic goods whose coverage will allow them to avoid engaging in harmful coping mechanisms, MHM and others), enabling them to meet their protection needs and mitigate their protection risks. UNHCR will directly implement this activity, informed by the results of the Protection Monitoring (see Activity 1). Referrals for this assistance will be made throughout the year by INGD and other capacitated national actors.Through these interventions, a total of some 30,900 drought affected people in the concerned districts of Sofala and Manica provinces will be targeted.
